   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Dr. E.J. Wilson, SURREY



Dear Brian,

Still plugging away at SAM. I'm
using clip art a lot, as small
pictures added to notes I put up
at the golf club. I'm the
Veterans Captain this year, so
have this privilege!!

However, try as I may, I am
unable to centre the pictures
when printing out. I use "Flash"
with the Small Dump but to get a
picture on the right of the
paper I have to resort to
inverting the picture then
reversing the printing paper.

The 'Flash' manual is awful and
despite 10 years with computers,
I am still hopeless at
programming and even at times
following instructions!

Can you help, please? Use any
part on OUTLET if you wish.

Happy New Year to you all at
OUTLET.

I tried using OUTDEX  but could
find nothing on this topic.

Keep up the good work.

        Yours sincerely,

         Dr. E.J. Wilson

Brian Cavers to Ted Wilson

What do you need to know about
OUTDEX?Instructions are in every
month under the heading "INDEX
DATA" but basically, you just
follow the prompts to load new
data then print the index.

To centre pictures printed from
FLASH you must change the left
margin and this you can do with
POKE 83234,X where X is the left
margin, that is, the number of
text characters from the left on
your printer at which the left
part of the picture will start.
For a small dump this is about
24 or 32. For a large dump it is
around 8. You need to exit to
BASIC to do this so..

In the original FLASH, take any
disc out of the drive and select
the QUIT option in the FILE sub-
menu. Wait a few seconds and you
should get an error message
"check disc in drive". Ignore
that; you are now in BASIC. If
you have a version of FLASH with
MENU at the bottom of the FILE
sub-menu then select that then
press ESC to get into BASIC. Now
enter...

 5 POKE 83234,8

and then type RUN and RETURN.You
should now be back in FLASH and
can try the DUMP. You'll have to
experiment a bit to get the
right number to centre the dump.
                        - Brian

 Derek Morgan, OLD SKELMERSDALE

From: Alan D. Cox, DYFED

In December's OUTBOARD,
W.P.Edwards wants 'Wordmaster'
and 'Typeliner' by Cardex, and
PCG's DTP. Does he realise that
PCG used to be Cardex, and the
DTP suite comprises 'Wordmaster'
'Typeliner' and 'Headliner'?

J.C.Clay (ADDENDERS 3) is having
trouble with FINANCE MANAGER and
his HR5 printer.I don't know the
program but assuming he has done
the appropriate POKE @6 if he is
using a Disciple or PLUS D, or
closed and opened channel 3 if a
SAM, then my guess is that
FINANCE MASTER is attempting a
graphics dump using ESC "*",n,
which of course the HR5 does not
support.

If there are BASIC parts of FM
then Mr Clay could look for
these command codes and
substitute ESC "K", or "L"
(together with switching between
Pica and Elite if he wants to).

If the dumping is done from
machine code then a simple BASIC
program to look for CHR$(27)
followed by CHR$(42) - and this
pair may occur several times -
would show if this is the
problem.

Does anyone know what, if
anything, the MOVE command does
in SAM's DOS? The SAM manual
points out that it only works
with disks but the only
documentation on Samdos I can
find does not cover it.

Does anyone know whether SAMCo
has produced new versions of the
standard SAM manual - my copy
says it was first published 1989
and is "Copyright MILES GORDON
TECHNOLOGY plc 1989". I know of
errors in this version, but
wonder if these were corrected
in later versions.


Have you seen SAMCo's latest
insult to our intelligence? No
more free newsletters. Instead
we are to be allowed the
privilege of paying initially
`1.00 per copy, then `2.50.
If we subscribe for three issues
`2.00 for a disk based advert-
isement. I believe that advert-
ising material should be free.

I never pay for plastic carrier
bags in supermarkets if they are
emblazoned with the store's name
etc. SAMCo should budget for
their advertising costs them-
selves. I have written to Alan
Miles telling him of my views.


I doubt you really need support
but entirely agree with your
comments in response to Mark
Broster's remark that OUTLET is
overpriced. I believe that it is
significantly under-priced when
compared to the competition.

Please do not take this as an
excuse to charge more or at
least not a lot more!

Let me now turn to my letter in
OUTLET 52 concerning Mike
Haine's excellent pair of
programs KEYMAP and KEYSET in
OUTLET 51. I found them useful
for two reasons. First, KEYMAP
'filled a long-felt want', and I
have run it and put a copy in
the back of my manual.

I am amazed that Mike expressed
any surprise that something
similar was not included in the
manual: the manual is a joke
however you look at it, and I am
no longer surprised at any of
its limitations - we just have
to learn to do without the
excellent standard of
documentation that we got with
the Spectrum - looking back on
it, it really was outstanding.

Mike's second program 'KEYSET'
was very useful to me because it
forced me to look again at the
SAM keyboard and the way it
works. I was unhappy with what
Mike said i.e. he was redefining
the codes of the KEYWORDS etc,
since I knew that this was not
possible, and after worrying at
the problem I now think I know
what is going on. What follows
is my understanding but clearly
I, and no doubt your other
readers, would welcome any
comments this letter provokes.

My earlier letter was sent off
in the first flush of finding a
way to get the 'lower set' of
tokens/keywords from a single
key.

With hindsight I should perhaps
have done a bit more research
before putting pen-to-paper (or
fingers-to-keys), but so be it.
I have now done a bit more work,
and can make what I think is a
more positive contribution.

As a result of trying to under-
stand my POKE and the various
points that Mike raises in his
letter and his two programs, I
now understand a lot more about
what is going on. I suspect that
I am not saying much, if any-
thing, that Mike has not already
said, but I have put things in a
way I can understand from my
simple point of view. Forgive me
if you find what follows pompous
and pedantic.

First, the function KEY x,y
takes x,which is the number
corresponding to any key
combination (including the three
special keys SHIFT, SYMBOL and
CONTROL) and produces a second
number y using the KEY look-up
table (LUT) at &58E0 to &59FF.
To express that a little better:
KEY assigns values to the KEY
LUT: the act of pressing any key
combination activates a read of
the LUT.

Normally this number y is then
taken as the code of either the
alphanumeric symbols if less
than 144 (roughly the same as
for the SPECTRUM, except for 127
to 143)or if above,the keywords
set out on page 66 of the
Technical Manual(Edition 3.0).

If the number y is 192 or more
(i.e. it has its first two bits
set) then a second look-up table
(the DEF KEYCODE LUT at &5800 to
&58DF)is used further to convert
y into z, where z can have a
(relatively) unlimited number of
bytes.

If there is no entry in the DEF
KEYCODE LUT then the original
assignment is used.

On switch on, the KEY LUT is set
up, which assigns non-zero
values y for nearly all key
combination numbers for bare
keys or for them together with
SHIFT or SYMBOL (but very few of
the combinations with CONTROL
are covered).

Incidentally, a minor mystery -
there are 72 keys on the SAM
keyboard, and three of these are
duplicated:SHIFT, SYMBOL and
full stop, so there are 69
independent key numbers. How-
ever, the diagram on page 180 of
the manual shows the bare key
numbers range from 1 to 70, so
one is missing - actually 9.

Presumably this means that
originally the  SAM keyboard was
intended to have one more key on
the keyboard - I wonder what it
was?    In addition, the DEF
KEYCODE LUT has values assigned
for 192 to 201 at switch on, and
also 252,253 and 254.(No doubt
there is a good reason for these
last three, but I cannot think
of one off hand).

Now since the KEY LUT only
caters for a single byte per key
number (it is so arranged that
the value for key number n is
the n'th entry (incidentally,
the manual says that key number
must be 0 to 279, whereas it is
actually 1 to 280) it is obvious
that KEY by itself cannot cover
the 'lower set' of keywords/
tokens which need a two-byte
code. This is where DEF KEYCODE
comes in since it allows several
bytes to be assigned to a
particular key number code.

The reason why my particular
POKE worked for F0 is that the
KEY LUT assigns the number 192
to F0 and the POKE then puts the
codes for PEEK in the DEF
KEYCODE LUT.

KEY LUT numbers for the function
keys and for the function keys +
SHIFT are shown on pages 178 and
179 of the manual,although until
now I did not realise what these
numbers meant. However, although
this allows SHIFT+F keys to do
something other than the obvious
there are no corresponding
entries in the DEF KEYCODE LUT
so nothing extra actually
happens. Thus,to enable a single
key to give one of the lower set
of keywords/tokens,several
things must be done. Firstly, it
is necessary to assign to the
key combination number a KEY LUT
value of 192 or above. Secondly,
it is necessary to assign in the
DEF KEYCODE LUT the appropriate
codes for the token/keyword
required.

The first step is easy - this is
done by KEY. The second is less
straightforward  and can be done
in two different ways.

You can POKE the DEF KEYCODE LUT
directly as I suggested in my
earlier letter but this mucks up
all the other DEF KEYCODE LUT
entries and would take a small
program to organize things
properly.

It is far better to use DEF
KEYCODE which does all the
housekeeping for you making sure
that changes to assignments do
not ruin everything else. DEF
KEYCODE has two separate modes,
depending upon whether you do
DEF KEYCODE n:or DEF KEYCODE n,.

As far as I have been able to
tell, with the colon you can
only use 'upper set' keywords/
tokens - like the PRINT "123"
example in the manual - whereas
there is no restriction when
used with the comma separator.


There are then two options viz
(i) POKE KEYCODE 192,"PEEK:" or
else DEF KEYCODE 192, CHR$(255)
+CHR$(97) +CHR$(58), and the
second of these is more economic
in the use of the limited DEF
KEYCODE LUT space (the actual
codes for keywords can be got
from the Technical Manual or
your CODELISTA program in OUTLET
33).

It seems to me the tidiest way
to implement the 'lower set' is
to leave other things as they
are and to use the CONTROL+key
combinations, most of which are
unassigned in the KEY LUT,
together with the function keys,
only the bare keys being
assigned in the DEF KEYCODE LUT,
with SHIFT+F key and SYMBOL+F
key being assigned in the KEY
LUT (although as pointed out
above, SHIFT+F key does nothing
useful) . In fact SYMBOL+F key
gives the numbers, like the F
keys in the number-pad mode, but
the number-pad mode appears not
to depend on KEY LUT assignments
-it must have its own data store
so you can reassign the SYMBOL+F
key numbers too. This gives 3*10
options, which should be enough.

I do not think Mike and I end up
at very different places, but
our routes are a bit different.
I can imagine a revised version
of Mike's KEYSET program but I
suspect that he might want to do
this himself.

                   Alan D. Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan D. Cox

The MOVE command in SAMDOS was
included for use with OPENTYPE
files but which were not implem-
ented, presumably either through
lack of space or more likely
because at the time there was
enormous pressure to get a dos,
ANY dos, available. Remember,the
dos was not ready when SAM was
launched so MGT had to pull out
all the stops to get it ready.

Regrettably,it is unlikely there
will be any further upgrade to
SAMDOS because MASTERDOS is now
available (this CAN use the MOVE
command). I say, "regrettably"
because MASTERDOS is copyright
and can never be the default dos
which everyone has.

Just to expand on that, fewer
programs will be written that
use the extra MASTERDOS commands
than use the standard because
only a certain percentage of all
SAM owners will every have
MASTERDOS so the target market
is smaller. With SAMDOS you KNOW
that your potential customer has
the dos but not with MASTERDOS.
For example, our STYLE WRITER
wordprocessor needs MASTERDOS so
it will only ever sell to a
smaller market whereas OUTWRITE
will work with any dos. My own
preference would be for SAMCo to
buy the rights to MASTERDOS and
allow it to be used freely just
like SAMDOS now is.It could then
be included on the disc of any
program that needed it.

No,SAMCO have not produced a new
version of the manual nor are
they likely to.Limited resources
have to be applied where they
will do the most good I guess.

SAMCo's NEWSDISK replaces the
HOTLINE as well as the news-
letter.I think they're justified
in making a charge because this
market is so small they do not
have the resources to throw
money at promotion. Remember,the
disc will have demos and, no
doubt, other things of interest,
including, so I hear, a serial-
ization of the ROM disassembly,
so most users should perceive
the disc to have more value than
the newsletter. In any case, if
it is not worth the money, users
won't buy it!          - Brian

From: G. Henderson, ABERDEEN

Dear Ron & Brian

I have been trying to LOAD
"OUTDEX" from OUTLET(SAM) 44 and
although it seemed to load O.K.
it will not read out correctly.
Title order reads to "REMOVER"
then stops with: "29 Not
understood,310:1". Issue order
and Subject order give a similar
result with error messages for
line 440 & 540 respectively.

OUTLETs 45 to 52 all LOADed OK
but still stalled on readout.
I've put it on my enclosed disc
so you can see what happens.
Please help, I need an index.

        Gordon Henderson

Brian Cavers to Gordon Henderson

This is a bug in the SAM Coupe's
ROM which affects the pageing of
memory in BASIC. Any BASIC that
is larger than about 9K may
suffer these problems because
BASIC starts in memory around
23765 so add 9K (=9216) and you
get 32981 which is just over the
first page boundary at 32768.The
problem re-occurs at the next
page boundary at 49152 and so on
but, of course, larger programs
are much rarer and so this comes
up less often.

The copies of OUTDEX you sent me
work perfectly on my SAM. This
indicates your SAM is different
to mine!

I must stress there is nothing
wrong with the programming in
OUTDEX - the fault is with the
SAM Coupe.What happens in OUTDEX
is that it is trying to READ
DATA and possibly the variables
it is trying to read or the DATA
itself is in a different page of
memory to the READ statement and
SAM is not pageing correctly. I
don't know whether it is the
BASIC or if, as I have heard, a
hardware problem in that pageing
is not quite fast enough in some
circumstances.

When writing a BASIC program,one
can often avoid the problem by
putting a dummy line at the top
of the listing to move the line
causing problem in memory...

Try adding...

3 IF 1=2 THEN PRINT 9,9,9,9,9,9

This line uses more memory (size
for size) than say, REM 999999
but, like REM, won't affect the
actual running of the program.

The problem with OUTDEX is even
more difficult because of course
new DATA is being added each
month and so the program is
growing and growing! An added
complexity is that different
people may not have EVERY issue
of OUTLET and therefore not have
ALL the DATA!We always check our
copy of the program each month
as we add DATA but clearly we
cannot make it foolproof! -Brian.

From: Ted Felstead, WIGAN

I've written a program called
'Plots2' as a follow up to plots
in order to cover more advanced
equations. Also, I'm sending a
program called 'Spirals'. I've
included this since I've become
aware, through reading back
issues,that every so often the
issue of copyright appears to
raise its head.

In particular the issue of Grant
Dixon's 'Megadem', (OUTLET 33)
caused me to think a bit as it
seemed that lots of the routines
were based on standard math-
ematical equations with changes
to variables in a random fashion
and then jazzed up a bit to make
them look pretty.

It surely is obvious that the
rules governing mathematics,
physics and chemistry are
universal and belong to no one.

I, in fact, wrote the 'Spirals'
program quite independently
before I saw 'Megadem' and was
intending to include it as part
of 'Plots3'. In fact the spiral
in one form or another has been
used in folklore down the ages,
in particular, the Celts used a
variation of the spiral in their
religion and I believe it has
been used by tribes all over the
world.

Also in Grant's offering were a
3D cube, random rectangles,
random circles, triangles and
ellipses.

I simply refuse to accept that
anyone, other than God himself,
could claim copyright to
material such as this.

I accept that special machine
code routines may have been
written to speed up the
execution but the fact still
remains that this type of
graphic display is a result of
symmetry in nature and can be
achieved easily by anyone.

Does anyone remember the child's
toy called a pantograph?. I had
one, many years ago, and I
achieved some very pretty, and
on the face of it, complex
graphics but so did millions of
others.

A few months ago, when Micronet
was still alive, I sent a very
small BASIC program to Brian
Gaff as a demo of how a simple
loop in a BASIC program could
achieve a quite complex result.

This program was not copied from
any other or extracted from a
listing but came about by
experimentation. The exact same
graphic appeared in 'Megadem'
but did not surprise me in the
least since it was a simple
mathematical equation with a
looped variable.

If it is allowed to claim copy-
right on variations of natural
laws then that spells the death
of all science since it has been

an accepted part or science over
the ages that free exchange of
ideas and information is the
only way that the human race can
step forward. Computers are, as
we all know, only calculating
machines. They are users of
mathematical equations and do
not themselves change the
fundamental laws of mathematics.

          Ted Felstead

Brian Cavers to Ted Felstead

You are absolutely right and I'm
glad you raised this point. I'm
sure that I speak absolutely for
Grant Dixon when I say that he
makes no claim of copyright in
mathematical routines when he
claims copyright for any program
using such routines. I'm sure
Grant would agree with me fully
and that it never occurred to
him to claim copyright in maths
routines. He is only claiming
copyright in the way he uses
them in his program. Even a line
of BASIC might be the same in
another program for example...
LET C = 2*PI*R otherwise how
could anyone calculate even the
circumference of a circle?

Even a sequence of lines may be
the same but the more complex,
the more unlikely two programs
will be EXACTLY the same.I think
I could soon tell if someone had
copied part of someone else's
program (or both had copied that
part from someone else), e.g.,
if all the variables have the
same names and the order is the
same etc.

I've not compared your two prog-
rams but I'm sure you've nothing
to worry about and you can claim
copyright in your own program if
you wish without stopping anyone
else using the same principles
of mathematics.

     - Pythagoras(Oi,YOU!)Cavers

           Mark Payne,
    5 Bassett Road, Coundon,
  COVENTRY, W. Midlands CV6 1LF

Dear Ron & Brian,

As you seem to know almost
everything about the Sinclair
computers I thought I would ask
you for some help.

I have a large collection of
records and I have been using
TASWORD 2 [on the Spectrum] to
keep a list of them but one
thing TASWORD cannot do is to
sort the entries in alphabetical
order. This would be of enormous
use as when I needed to find a
record I would not have to sort
through my entire list to find a
particular item.

If you would include my address
so other people can reply to my
letter, I'd be most grateful.

Also as a new member to OUTLET I
have noticed that it is 80% for
the serious user. Would you be
willing to include a large,good-
quality game in your issues (say
once every 3 months).

           Mark Payne


Brian Cavers to Mark Payne

Yes, I'm willing! You send 'em,
I'll put 'em in! Seriously, we
can only publish what is sent to
us. I have less and less time to
write large programs myself so I
cannot apply myself to this. As
it stands anyway, we often have
games: BREAKTHRU' (Issue 21),
CARNIVAL CAPERS (16),COLOUR BIND
(25), GLOBULAR TROUBLE (29),
GOLDEN COBRA (18), KEMSHU (23),
SHANGHAI (24), SPIN IT (26),
TRAILRACER (47), TRAKTRAP (15),
ULTIMATE WARRIOR (41), WITCHWOOD
3D (19), SANTA (52) and loads
and loads more!If you mean games
that could sell for `9.99 and
earn thousands of pounds then we
await such with bated breath!

Regarding sorting your Tasword 2
files this might not be too
difficult if each item to be
sorted uses the same number of
lines. We have such a program in
our SAM version (SELECTSORT in
OUTLET 40). Please send one of
your files for me to look at as
a lot depends on how it is set
out. Do you put one item on each
line? Is the name to be sorted
at the start of the line or in
the middle? Are there any gaps
between lines?

Instead of Tasword 2, what you
should have used is a database(a
record-keeping program) which
would sort them how you like.
Still, it may be possible to
sort them as they are.
                      - Brian

From: Bob Nutley, BOREHAMWOOD

Dear Ron and Brian,

I wish to renew my subscription
to your excellent mag. It takes
me a week to read it. I would
also like to order a copy of
OUTWRITE and a copy of STYLE
WRITER. Please keep up the good
work. The SAM needs all the
support it can get.

Is there any chance of a 3-D
construction kit dedicated to
SAM? I feel that a really first
class game-creator (tool kit)
and a windows-type desktop would
really put the SAM on the map.

                    Bob Nutley

Brian Cavers to Bob Nutley

You're not the only person to
think that a games-creator would
really put SAM on the map.I hear
strong rumours that Andy Wright
may be working on such a utility
and presumably this will be an
extension to BASIC. I think STOS
and AMOS on the ST and AMIGA
include a "games-language" that
is similar to BASIC.

I doubt that 3D CONSTRUCTION KIT
will be converted for SAM but
the Spectrum version runs fine
under EMUTILITY (OUTLET 34). You
can save the whole thing to disc
while developing a game then do
a snapshot for the final thing
after making a temporary save on
tape.

You can get a SAM conversion of
the Spectrum DTP Pack from PCG,
61 School Street, Barrow-in-
Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW for
`37.95. This is limited to Mode
1 screens but most of the clip
art that is around is Mode 1 and
the program is very good anyway.

I think SAM BASIC is powerful
enough to do a WINDOWS environ-
ment at least as good as the ST
and rather better. I would like
to do this myself but have not
had time. A direct BASIC command
line is not really suited for
searching sub-directories; in
fact it's a real pain at times!

                        - Brian.

From: Dr. E.J. Wilson, SURREY

Dear Brian,

My earlier letter was sent off in the first flush of finding a way to get the 'lower set' of tokens/keywords from a single key.

To express that a little better: KEY assigns values to the KEY LUT: the act of pressing any key combination activates a read of the LUT.

Normally this number y is then taken as the code of either the alphanumeric symbols if less than 144 (roughly the same as for the SPECTRUM, except for 127 to 143)or if above,the keywords set out on page 66 of the Technical Manual(Edition 3.0).

If the number y is 192 or more (i.e. it has its first two bits set) then a second look-up table (the DEF KEYCODE LUT at &5800 to &58DF)is used further to convert y into z, where z can have a (relatively) unlimited number of bytes.

If there is no entry in the DEF KEYCODE LUT then the original assignment is used.

On switch on, the KEY LUT is set up, which assigns non-zero values y for nearly all key combination numbers for bare keys or for them together with SHIFT or SYMBOL (but very few of the combinations with CONTROL are covered).

Incidentally, a minor mystery - there are 72 keys on the SAM keyboard, and three of these are duplicated:SHIFT, SYMBOL and full stop, so there are 69 independent key numbers. How- ever, the diagram on page 180 of the manual shows the bare key numbers range from 1 to 70, so one is missing - actually 9.

Presumably this means that originally the  SAM keyboard was intended to have one more key on the keyboard - I wonder what it was?    In addition, the DEF KEYCODE LUT has values assigned for 192 to 201 at switch on, and also 252,253 and 254.(No doubt there is a good reason for these last three, but I cannot think of one off hand).

Now since the KEY LUT only caters for a single byte per key number (it is so arranged that the value for key number n is the n'th entry (incidentally, the manual says that key number must be 0 to 279, whereas it is actually 1 to 280) it is obvious that KEY by itself cannot cover the 'lower set' of keywords/ tokens which need a two-byte code. This is where DEF KEYCODE comes in since it allows several bytes to be assigned to a particular key number code.

The reason why my particular POKE worked for F0 is that the KEY LUT assigns the number 192 to F0 and the POKE then puts the codes for PEEK in the DEF KEYCODE LUT.

KEY LUT numbers for the function keys and for the function keys + SHIFT are shown on pages 178 and 179 of the manual,although until now I did not realise what these numbers meant. However, although this allows SHIFT+F keys to do something other than the obvious there are no corresponding entries in the DEF KEYCODE LUT so nothing extra actually happens. Thus,to enable a single key to give one of the lower set of keywords/tokens,several things must be done. Firstly, it is necessary to assign to the key combination number a KEY LUT value of 192 or above. Secondly, it is necessary to assign in the DEF KEYCODE LUT the appropriate codes for the token/keyword required.

The first step is easy - this is done by KEY. The second is less straightforward  and can be done in two different ways.

You can POKE the DEF KEYCODE LUT directly as I suggested in my earlier letter but this mucks up all the other DEF KEYCODE LUT entries and would take a small program to organize things properly.

It is far better to use DEF KEYCODE which does all the housekeeping for you making sure that changes to assignments do not ruin everything else. DEF KEYCODE has two separate modes, depending upon whether you do DEF KEYCODE n:or DEF KEYCODE n,.

As far as I have been able to tell, with the colon you can only use 'upper set' keywords/ tokens - like the PRINT "123" example in the manual - whereas there is no restriction when used with the comma separator.

There are then two options viz (i) POKE KEYCODE 192,"PEEK:" or else DEF KEYCODE 192, CHR$(255) +CHR$(97) +CHR$(58), and the second of these is more economic in the use of the limited DEF KEYCODE LUT space (the actual codes for keywords can be got from the Technical Manual or your CODELISTA program in OUTLET 33).

It seems to me the tidiest way to implement the 'lower set' is to leave other things as they are and to use the CONTROL+key combinations, most of which are unassigned in the KEY LUT, together with the function keys, only the bare keys being assigned in the DEF KEYCODE LUT, with SHIFT+F key and SYMBOL+F key being assigned in the KEY LUT (although as pointed out above, SHIFT+F key does nothing useful) . In fact SYMBOL+F key gives the numbers, like the F keys in the number-pad mode, but the number-pad mode appears not to depend on KEY LUT assignments -it must have its own data store so you can reassign the SYMBOL+F key numbers too. This gives 3*10 options, which should be enough.

This is a bug in the SAM Coupe's ROM which affects the pageing of memory in BASIC. Any BASIC that is larger than about 9K may suffer these problems because BASIC starts in memory around 23765 so add 9K (=9216) and you get 32981 which is just over the first page boundary at 32768.The problem re-occurs at the next page boundary at 49152 and so on but, of course, larger programs are much rarer and so this comes up less often.

I don't know whether it is the BASIC or if, as I have heard, a hardware problem in that pageing is not quite fast enough in some circumstances.

When writing a BASIC program,one can often avoid the problem by putting a dummy line at the top of the listing to move the line causing problem in memory...

Try adding...

3 IF 1=2 THEN PRINT 9,9,9,9,9,9

Простите меня, если вы найдете то, что следует, напыщенным и педантичным.

Во-первых, функция KEY x,y берет x, который является числом, соответствующим любой комбинации клавиш (включая три специальные клавиши SHIFT, SYMBOL и CONTROL), и создает второе число y, используя таблицу поиска KEY (LUT) по адресам &58E0 – &59FF. Чтобы выразить это немного лучше: KEY присваивает значения таблице KEY LUT: действие нажатия любой комбинации клавиш активирует чтение таблицы LUT.

Обычно это число y затем принимается как код либо буквенно-цифровых символов, если оно меньше 144 (примерно так же, как для SPECTRUM, за исключением 127–143), либо, если больше, ключевых слов, изложенных на странице 66 Технического руководства (издание 3.0).

Если число y равно 192 или больше (т.е. у него установлены первые два бита), то для преобразования y в z используется вторая таблица поиска (DEF KEYCODE LUT по адресам &5800 – &58DF), где z может иметь (относительно) неограниченное количество байтов.

Если в таблице DEF KEYCODE LUT нет записи, используется исходное назначение.

При включении таблица KEY LUT настраивается, присваивая ненулевые значения y почти для всех номеров комбинаций клавиш для отдельных клавиш или вместе с SHIFT или SYMBOL (но покрывается очень мало комбинаций с CONTROL).

Кстати, небольшая загадка — на клавиатуре SAM 72 клавиши, и три из них дублируются: SHIFT, SYMBOL и точка, так что есть 69 независимых номеров клавиш. Однако диаграмма на странице 180 руководства показывает, что номера клавиш для отдельных нажатий варьируются от 1 до 70, так что одного не хватает — на самом деле 9.

По-видимому, это означает, что изначально на клавиатуре SAM предполагалось наличие еще одной клавиши — интересно, какой? Кроме того, таблица DEF KEYCODE LUT имеет значения, назначенные для 192–201 при включении, а также 252, 253 и 254. (Несомненно, есть веская причина для этих последних трех, но я не могу придумать ее навскидку).

Поскольку таблица KEY LUT обслуживает только один байт на номер клавиши (она организована так, что значение для клавиши номер n является n-й записью (кстати, в руководстве сказано, что номер клавиши должен быть от 0 до 279, тогда как на самом деле от 1 до 280)), очевидно, что KEY сама по себе не может покрыть «нижний набор» ключевых слов/токенов, которым нужен двухбайтовый код. Вот тут-то и вступает в игру DEF KEYCODE, поскольку она позволяет назначать несколько байтов определенному коду номера клавиши.

Причина, по которой мой конкретный POKE сработал для F0, заключается в том, что таблица KEY LUT назначает число 192 для F0, а POKE затем помещает коды для PEEK в таблицу DEF KEYCODE LUT.

### Клавиши и функции

Номера KEY LUT для функциональных клавиш, а также для комбинаций функциональных клавиш с SHIFT, приведены на страницах 178 и 179 руководства, хотя до сих пор я не осознавал, что эти числа означают. Однако, несмотря на то, что это позволяет клавишам SHIFT+F выполнять действия, отличные от очевидных, в DEF KEYCODE LUT нет соответствующих записей, поэтому фактически ничего дополнительного не происходит. Таким образом, чтобы одна клавиша вызывала одно из ключевых слов/токенов из нижнего набора, необходимо выполнить несколько условий. Во-первых, необходимо присвоить номеру комбинации клавиш значение KEY LUT, равное 192 или выше. Во-вторых, необходимо присвоить в DEF KEYCODE LUT соответствующие коды для требуемого токена/ключевого слова.

Первый шаг прост — это делается с помощью KEY. Второй шаг менее прямолинеен, и его можно выполнить двумя разными способами.

Вы можете напрямую выполнить POKE в DEF KEYCODE LUT, как я предлагал в своем предыдущем письме, но это нарушит все остальные записи DEF KEYCODE LUT, и для приведения всего в порядок потребуется небольшая программа.

Гораздо лучше использовать DEF KEYCODE, который берет на себя всю внутреннюю работу, гарантируя, что изменения назначений не испортят всё остальное. DEF KEYCODE имеет два отдельных режима, в зависимости от того, используете ли вы `DEF KEYCODE n:` или `DEF KEYCODE n,`.

Насколько я смог понять, с двоеточием можно использовать только «верхний набор» ключевых слов/токенов — как в примере с PRINT "123" в руководстве, — тогда как при использовании с разделителем-запятой ограничений нет.

Существует два варианта, а именно: (i) `POKE KEYCODE 192,"PEEK:"` или `DEF KEYCODE 192, CHR$(255)+CHR$(97)+CHR$(58)`. Второй вариант более экономен в использовании ограниченного пространства DEF KEYCODE LUT (фактические коды для ключевых слов можно получить из Technical Manual или вашей программы CODELISTA в OUTLET 33).

Мне кажется, самый аккуратный способ реализовать «нижний набор» — оставить всё остальное как есть и использовать комбинации CONTROL+клавиша (большинство из которых не назначены в KEY LUT) вместе с функциональными клавишами. При этом в DEF KEYCODE LUT назначаются только обычные клавиши, а SHIFT+F и SYMBOL+F назначаются в KEY LUT (хотя, как было сказано выше, SHIFT+F не делает ничего полезного). На самом деле SYMBOL+F выдает цифры, как F-клавиши в режиме цифровой клавиатуры, но этот режим, по-видимому, не зависит от назначений KEY LUT — у него должно быть собственное хранилище данных, поэтому вы можете переназначить и цифры для SYMBOL+F. Это дает 3*10 вариантов, чего должно быть достаточно.

### Брайан Каверс — Гордону Хендерсону

Это ошибка в ПЗУ SAM Coupe, которая влияет на переключение страниц памяти в BASIC. Любой BASIC размером более 9 КБ может страдать от этих проблем, потому что BASIC запускается в памяти примерно с адреса 23765, добавляем 9 КБ (=9216) и получаем 32981, что чуть выше границы первой страницы 32768. Проблема повторяется на следующей границе страницы 49152 и так далее, но, конечно, программы большего объема встречаются гораздо реже, и поэтому это происходит реже.

Копии OUTDEX, которые вы мне прислали, отлично работают на моем SAM. Это указывает на то, что ваш SAM отличается от моего!

Должен подчеркнуть, что в программировании OUTDEX нет ничего неправильного — ошибка в самом SAM Coupe. В OUTDEX происходит попытка чтения данных (READ DATA), и, возможно, переменные, которые он пытается прочитать, или сами данные находятся на другой странице памяти, нежели оператор READ, и SAM переключает страницы неправильно. Я не знаю, дело ли в самом BASIC или, как я слышал, это аппаратная проблема, при которой переключение страниц в некоторых обстоятельствах происходит недостаточно быстро.

При написании программы на BASIC часто можно избежать этой проблемы, добавив фиктивную строку в начале листинга, чтобы сместить проблемную строку в памяти...

Попробуйте добавить...

```text
3 IF 1=2 THEN PRINT 9,9,9,9,9,9
```

Эта строка занимает больше памяти (по размеру), чем, скажем, REM 999999, но, как и REM, она не повлияет на фактическое выполнение программы.

Проблема с OUTDEX еще сложнее, потому что, конечно, новые данные добавляются каждый месяц, и программа растет и растет! Дополнительная сложность в том, что у разных людей могут быть не все выпуски OUTLET, и, следовательно, не все данные! Мы всегда проверяем нашу копию программы каждый месяц, когда добавляем данные, но ясно, что мы не можем сделать её защищенной от дурака! - Brian.
